reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes purchasing BitClub Network membership and mining-pool packages, directs viewers through Bitcoin payments, and presents the opportunity as an easy way to build Bitcoin earnings. He also promotes recruitment-based income, citing commissions from his team and encouraging viewers to join and build the business. The video therefore contains a concrete solicitation involving payment and claimed financial returns, rather than merely reporting on the service.

citations.quote: setting up an account and buying a mining, a mining pool package within the Bitcoin network
$99 is one-time membership fee and the $500 obviously goes into the mining pool investment
its gonna repurchase bitcoin on a daily basis with 100% of his earns
I'm looking to mine at 100% for at least 9 to 12 months so I can acquire as much bitcoin as I can through the mining pool share

opening.argument: The presentation is materially qualified rather than framed as a certainty. The speaker admits, "I don't claim to be an expert in this business yet," cautions that viewers "may get a few challenges with it," and describes his own approach as a personal choice: "I think it's best to leave it 100 for a few months." Those qualifications make this a personal, fallible account of using a service, not an unequivocal promise that viewers will profit. The evidence supports an operational explanation accompanied by uncertainty, which fits an educational technology or business demonstration.

citations.quote: I don't claim to be an expert in this business yet
you may get a few challenges with it but once you've done it once it's very very easy
but i think it's best to leave it 100 for a few months just to build it up a little bit quicker

rebuttal.rebuttal: The payment walkthrough establishes that an account was being configured, but it does not establish a guarantee of returns. Likewise, the statement about repurchasing Bitcoin describes a selected account setting, while the speaker expressly acknowledges possible challenges and limited expertise. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether the presentation is deceptive rather than merely promotional and experiential.

citations.quote: its gonna repurchase bitcoin on a daily basis with 100% of his earns
you may get a few challenges with it
I don't claim to be an expert in this business yet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer of expertise is not a risk disclosure about the purchaser's money, and saying users may face challenges still calls the process "very very easy." The same speaker directs the membership and package purchases and describes acquiring Bitcoin through the pool, so modest caveats do not remove the financial solicitation.

citations.quote: you may get a few challenges with it but once you've done it once it's very very easy
$99 is one-time membership fee and the $500 obviously goes into the mining pool investment
so I can acquire as much bitcoin as I can through the mining pool share

opening.argument: The video's central activity is a screen-level operational demonstration: logging into an account, opening order history, scanning Bitcoin payment codes, and configuring mining-pool percentages. The speaker narrates the steps, including setting up a Coinbase wallet and completing a transaction, rather than offering an abstract promise. He explicitly presents it as help with another person's account: "I'm going to pay the 99 dollar membership for him" and later says he "helped my friend out." That concrete how-to format supports classifying the content as an operational tutorial or demonstration.

citations.quote: I'm gonna pay the 99 dollar membership for him
what you do is set up an account yours, upload your passport, and your utility bill
I helped my friend out you're just he's on holidays at the moment
set this mining pool one which is the one he's just bought into and set this to 100%

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a walkthrough does not change what viewers can learn from it: the walkthrough shows how to pay for membership and a mining package. The narration also goes beyond neutral interface orientation by discussing how to configure earnings, but a demonstration can still be educational without proving that the underlying service delivers the suggested results.

citations.quote: setting up an account and buying a mining, a mining pool package
We've got a choice of four packages more or less five hundred a thousand two thousand or the founders package
set this mining pool one which is the one he's just bought into and set this to 100%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The interface tutorial is not merely technical: it tells viewers how to transfer Bitcoin for a membership and mining-pool package, then recommends retaining all earnings for months to accumulate more Bitcoin. Demonstrating the transaction is precisely what makes the solicitation actionable; an educational format does not neutralize the financial claims accompanying it.

citations.quote: I have to pay this $99 dollar membership fee with bitcoin
five hundred dollars like I said he's already paid me to five hundred dollars so I'm going to buy this package from them
I'm looking to mine at 100% for at least 9 to 12 months so I can acquire as much bitcoin as I can

opening.argument: The supplied material is consistent with an ordinary paid membership and a service purchase: it identifies a one-time membership fee, lists several package levels, and records orders as paid or pending within the member portal. The speaker explains the payment route and account controls, but the record does not establish a guaranteed return, a required downline, or that the service is unsafe. His mention of team commissions is a report about his own participation, not a clear instruction that viewers must recruit others. On this evidence, the safest classification is ordinary commerce or service promotion, without certifying the provider's claims.

citations.quote: $99 is one-time membership fee and the $500 obviously goes into the mining pool investment
We've got a choice of four packages more or less five hundred a thousand two thousand or the founders package
I think I've brought in about 29 or 10 people
I am get any 18 percent Commissions now on a daily Basis from my Team

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of prices and an order history is evidence of a commercial transaction, not by itself evidence of a scam mechanism. The speaker's personal commission report does not clearly tell the audience to recruit, and the cited material does not prove a guaranteed outcome or a deceptive promise. The prosecution's interpretation adds conclusions that the operational record alone does not establish.

citations.quote: I am get any 18 percent Commissions now on a daily Basis from my Team
you can change this to 50 if you want and start to withdraw bitcoin every day if you want

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Ordinary pricing does not make an investment solicitation ordinary retail commerce. The speaker says $500 goes into a mining-pool investment, describes daily Bitcoin repurchases from earnings, and reports commissions from his team. These are financial-return and recruitment-linked features, even if the evidence does not prove every possible mechanism or guarantee.
